div.p: Recent progress in network technologies has made it possible to integrate digital video and audio into distributed computing environments. Among the distributed multimedia applications, the Video-On-Demand(V0D) service is the most typical application area. However, the interest on the large-scale VOD system is gradually transferring to the small and lowcost VOD system because of the excess investment for the transmission media.

When we make a small-scale VOD system, one of the most important factor is the eflcient resource management of the VOD server in order to achieve cost effectiveness. Thus, multimedia has generated widespread interest in real-time and high performance I.0 support within general purpose operating systems.

This paper presents the performance of the smallscale VOD server based on the WiX equipped with the real-time scheduler and the continuous media file system(CA4FS). The real-time scheduler is based on the theory for non-preemptive real-time to test schedulability within polynomial time. To reduce interference of the interrupt processing for the real-time process, the realtime processes are classified into two groups in order of the importance. The CMFS have been designed and implemented to acquire the performance of the raw disk, According to the analysis of the measured data, the WiX can eflciently transfer the video data @om the disk to network, and the W I X can also guarantee most of deadline.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Until recently, we have believed that the ATM technology and the data compression technology enable the transmission of the video stream to thousands of subscribers. But, the results of experimental services have showed that the VOD service is not adequate in current environment because it requires the excess investments for the network.
There is much interest in a small-scale VOD system.
In most cases, a small-scale VOD system is runed in the LAN environment.

To enable LAN-wide VOD service, we must begin the design and implementation of VOD server. In general, a video server must address the following issues [ 151 : high storage capacity, minimum response time, quality of service, cost effectiveness, real-time requirements, VCR-like API. These issues require us to focus on designing I/O subsystem and real-time facilities.

The digital video fundamentally requires high performance hardware and an efficient operating system. In operating system context, digital video requires the soft-timelineness. This is why the users can accept the video naturally although video servers degrade QOS during the system is overloaded. Therefore, we can use the general-purpose operating system if the several functional requirements are included. Unfortunately, previous research doesn't focus on operating systems. 'This kind of trend disregarding operating systems as one of the solutions to service the VOD application can be analyzed in three ways.

The first reason is that the resource utilization wasn't important in a commercial aspect. Resources in a system could easily be upgraded privately. They are different from the network bandwidth which is shared by the public.
The second is that the previous research focused on middlewares and applications.
The third is that the continuous media applications was closely connected to specific hardwares and operating systems.
This paper describes the performance of the smallscale VOD server based on the UNIX. We have added more facilities to the UNIX. Table 1 depicts the functions included in the UNIX.
This paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we describe the details of the small-scale VOD server. Section 3 summarizes the experimental environment.
The performance of the small-scale VOD server is discussed in Section 4. Section 6 concludes the paper.

div.head: PI. THE SMALL-SCALE VIDEO SERVER
div.p: The small-scale VOD system consists of a video server, an access network and a collection of client equipped with MPEG decoder, web browser as user interface, and TV(or overlay board). Figure 1 illustrates the overall architecture of the small-scale VOD system. The dotted circle of Figure 1 depicts the internal operation of the video server. The video server can be divided into two subsystems. The first subsystem is the CMFS(Continuous Media File System). The CMFS is a file system designed for storage and retrieval of video files. The CMFS supports a very large logical block, predictable data block search and optimized data transfer. The performance of the CMFS is more enhanced by the software disk striping.

The second subsystem is the real-time scheduler and the pumping threads. The pumping threads are disk I/O thread and network I/O thread. The disk I/O thread generates disk-requests for reading digital video data from the disks. The network 110 threads send video streams to clients. These operations are performed
periodically. The periodic real-time scheduler is responsible for guaranteeing time coastraints of all threads. The real-time scheduler )uses the nonpreemptive EDF algorithm.

div.head: Dual Deadline Non-preemptive EDF Scheduler
div.p: In the aspect of real-time schedulling theory, the pumping threads have some problems. 'Operation of the pumping threads are non-preemptive because they are closely related to the driver module. There is a producer/consumer relationship between the disk I/O thread and the network I/O thread.
In our VOD server, we apply thle dual deadline concept and the scheduablity test technique of nonpreemptive thread to the earliest deadline first(EDF) scheduling algorithm.

div.head: The Schedulable Condition
div.p: It is well known that the schedulability problem for non-preemptive threads is NP-complete in strong sense. Therefore, non-preemptive threads can't always be guaranteed without imposing some restrictions on their time requirement. The basic idea of this paper is that we confine the upper bound of the computing time to prevent the priority inversion. Intuitively, the thread with the shortest period is the most sensitive to the priority inversion. So, we set the computing time of the thread based on the computing time of the shortest period thread. The theorem applied to a small VOD server is shown below. The proof for the theorem is already published in [21].

The above theorem can test schedulability with O( 1 ) . That is, we test schedulability by examining only the current load, the request processor utilization ratio, and the amount of the computing time a period.

The determination of start time for an arrived thread is also easy because we restrict the start time in the above theorem. However, we can not guarantee the schedulability in real world because the UNIX isn't fully preemptive and the variance of the computing time is dependent on the system status. The following paragraph describes the dual-deadline concepts that give priority to the more important thread. The continuous media application can consist of several threads to compose a processing chain. In this environment, the continuous media application may not serve continuous video stream if the cost of the deadline miss is expensive. In the example in Figure 2, the deadline miss of the display thread immediately affects the quality of application. Therefore, we can divide the importance of deadline into two classes. In other words, the deadline can be distinguished according to effectiveness of the deadline miss. In this paper, we analyze two kinds of deadlines : the external deadline which has an effect on the quality of the application and the internal deadline which doesn't have an effect on the quality of the application. ?he thread that has the external deadline takes priority over the thread that has the internal deadline, while the system is overloaded for a while. If two threads should perform at the same time, the external deadline thread is executed regardless of an emergency of internal deadline thread. This approach considers the peripheral device, and simplifies the real-time scheduling during the system is overloaded.

div.head: Stream Storage
div.p: Our stream storage consists of the CMFS and the disk striping driver. The CMFS is a read-oriented file system that support a very large file system block, predictable data block search and optimized data transfer.

div.head: Continuous Media File System
div.p: The video server must have the capacity to store a large number of videos because one hour video occupies approximately 3-4 GBytes of storage when compressed into a MPEG-2 type. Thus, a storage architecture for a video server must address the following issues : low-cost, continuous retrieval of movies, VCR-like operation. Thus, the first step to design the stream storage is designing a new file system that can support multimedia applications.
The CMFS have its own structure to support VOD application. Table 2 summarize the structural difference when the regular file system such as ufs and s5fs are compared with the CMFS.

div.head: Software Disk Striping
div.p: When high performance I/O is need, we can use disk striping technique. There are 3 levels of RAID implementation : software level, host bus controller level and subsystem controller level. In our stream storage, the disk driver performs the disk striping. The advantages of software disk striping are low cost and high performance while the disadvantages of the software disk striping are the fact that we can not use hot' and redundant technologies. environments. Our implementation is on the general PC server running the UnixWare 2.01. The machine is equipped with 133 MHz Pentium, 2 SCSI controller and 82Mbyte memories. For our evaluation, we used the wide SCSI disk with the parameters listed in Table 3.

div.head: IV. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
div.p: This section describes the experimental results for the small VOD server based on the UNIX. We outline the predictability of the real-time scheduler and the performance of the VOD server.

div.head: Predictability
div.p: The time interiupt resolution determines the granularity of the allocation unit of the processor time. The finer the time interrupt resolution is, the smaller the allocation unit of the processor is. In our environment, we have increased the time interrupt resolution from 100 Hz to 1 OOOHz. The performance degradation by the increased clock interrupt processing was 3 YO.

To support a predictable real-time scheduling facility, the reserved processor time of thread should be consumed without interference. A thread must not exceed its allocated processor time and must not be removed.

In order to measure the degree of predictability, we must measure the effect of interference while running a compute-bounded thread(CBT) with 5Omsec period and 25msec computational time(50% prolcessor time).

First, we run only CBT. In this experiment, we can measure the interference effect of system daemon and periodic interrupt handler for 8950nnsec. According to the experimental data, the reserved processor time is consumed by the CBT. That is, the nonreal-time system daemon and periodic interrupt handler don't interfere with the CBT. That is why the real-time thread has the highest priority execpt for the interrupt handler and why the periodic interrupt handler consumes onlt serveral usecs. According to the graph of Figure 4, the interrupt handler has stolen the CBT's 88mses pirocessor time for 4475msec. The ratio of the interferlence is 1.9%. The amount of the interference is very small. We have also measured the interference from 5 disk 1/0 threads. The measurement showed that the 2.01% of the CBT's processor time was removed.

As the above result show, there is little interference of disk I/O threads. but, the scheduler can't guarantee the computing time if a thread lhas a very small computing time such as several msecs. When the operating system can not support real-time facilities completely, the small-quantum threads should be clustered to guarantee the computing time. Lastly, Figure 5 shows the ratio of CBT's processor time when the 6Mbps network transmission is performed as a background process. The consumed processor time of CBT is varied randomly. This is because the network protocol processing of UnixWare is driven by the stream scheduling on interrupt context. That is, the network transmission process only generate the network I/O request to the stream module of the operating systems. The UnixWare can't guarantee the allocated processor time of process because the interrupt have a higher priority than all user and kernel process. In our experiments, the network transmission process have taken away 10 % of CBT's processor time. Thus, the process that has several msecs of computing time, may starve by the network protocol processing.

This result points out the demerit of the general purpose operating system. The modified UNIX was effective in making performance more predictable, but the level of predictability was not suitable for multimedia application. In order to make predictable environments, all processing should be done on user context. That is, the network protocol processing should be done in the user context.

div.head: The Performance of the Dual Deadline EDF Scheduling
div.p: The performance of the Dual Deadline EDF scheduling is measured by the deadline miss ratios of the network I/O threads when the disk I/O threads generate the disk-request at 6 Mbps. However, the network I/O threads generate the load. But the generated network I/O is removed immediately. We do not consider the network protocol processing because the interrupt processing by the network interferes with the real-time threads severely The performance of Dual Deadline EDF scheduling is compared to the EDF scheduling. The number of session is increased from 7 to 10. Table 4 shows the deadline miss ratio of the network 110 threads. The number in Table 4 is the number of the deadline miss. And the number in the parenthesis of Table 4 is the ratios of the deadline miss. The difference of the deadline miss ratios increase as the system load is increased. And when the 10 sessions is served, the difference of the deadline miss ratios increased grately According to these results, the Dual Deadline EDF scheduling is more suitable for the soft-real time application on the general purpose operating systems. div.head: Bandwidth of CMFS
div.p: We have assumed each request for the disk read is generated continuously after one request is processed. Figure 7 shows the CMFS bandwidth while varying the size of the logical block. The one unit of load generator read the file from the CMFS continuously. When the size of the CMFS is 256Kbytes, the bandwidth of the CMFS approaches to that of the raw disk. The logical block guarantees the minimum sequential read. Thus, we can get a higher performance as the size of the logical block is increases. In Figure 8, we show the graphs of the best performance for each disk configuration. "2 disk(256/2048) + 1 controller" means that the striping disk consists of two disks which are connected to one controller and the size of logical block is 256 Kbytes and the striping unit is 2048 Kbytes. The graph shows a good scalability. So, the software disk striping can be a candidate for a secondary storage of the video server. The striping unit of most of the graph is Erom 256k to 2048k. This means that the concurrency is more important than the parallelism to support the video server.

The variance of the throughput was increased as the size of the logical disk block is larger. To satisfy high and stable disk bandwidth we properly choose the size of the disk block. According to our measurements, the proper size of the logical disk block is from 128Kbytes to 256Kbytes. The striping unit doesn't directly affect the variance of the throughput if the logical disk block is properly chosen. However, the striping unit which is larger than 2048Kbytes cause concurrency-miss. The number of disk are selected by considering the capacity of the video server and the disk failure.

div.head: Overall performance
div.p: Despite the storage system can support 3 1 sessions, the network subsytem can support 5 sessions. Thus, the small video server can support 5 sessions of 6 Mbps. This is mainly because the network protocol processing require a number of computing power.

According to the overall performance measurements, it is difficult to support VOD service on the general purpose operating system environment. But if the following problem is resolved, we might begin the VOD service.
First, the more processing power is needed to process the network protocol.
Second, the interrupt handler that requires long computing time, disturb the real-time scheduling.
Lastly, the network bandwidth is not enough even if the ATM technology is used.

div.head: V. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper we discussed an approach to support VOD service using general-purpose operating systems. Also, we considered the integration of disk, real-time scheduler and the characteristics of threads.
The extended features of the operating system in experimental environments are the real-time scheduler and the CMFS.

The results of performance measurements show that the network protocol processing is a source of nonpredictability. High performance processor should be used to process the network protocol. However, the performance of the storage system was not a problem to do VOD service. Thus, the real-time features and the high performance processsor should be supported to general-purpose general-purpose operating system because the upper bound of the session is mainly determined by the method o f network protocol processing.
